title: Small-site transport of the first-residue pushout
statement:
theorem internal_first_residue_smallMap_pushout
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    {R B S : Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1}}
    [MonObj R] [MonObj B] [MonObj S]
    [IsCommMonObj R] [IsCommMonObj B] [IsCommMonObj S]
    (f : R ⟶ B) [IsMonHom f] (q : R ⟶ S) [IsMonHom q]
    (p : B ⟶ S) [IsMonHom p]
    (h : IsPushout f q p (𝟙 _)) :
    IsPushout (IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X f)
      (IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X q)
      (IntegralModelsStacks.smallMap X p) (𝟙 _)

proof.text: In the preadditive category of abelian sheaves, f is epi. Indeed, if f ≫ g = 0, the pushout descendent for (g, 0) is zero because its composite with the identity lower edge is zero. Its composite with p is g, hence g = 0. Apply Preadditive.epi_of_cancel_zero.

The section-ring reconstruction forgets definitionally to the original additive sheaf and additive map. The faithful functor sheafCompose with forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat ⋙ forget₂ RingCat Ab reflects epimorphisms, so sectionMap X f is epi. Both AsSmall.down and AsSmall.up are continuous for the transported topology. Apply Adjunction.sheafPushforwardContinuous to the inverse AsSmall equivalence adjunction. Thus the small-site pushforward is a left adjoint and preserves epimorphisms, so smallMap X f is epi.

Apply the small-site pushforward functor to the reconstructed equality f ≫ p = q from the original commutative square. This gives the required commutative square with lower identity. Apply Mathlib IsPushout.of_horiz_isIso_epi to its epi top edge and identity lower edge.

proof_origin.place: section-ring reconstruction and AsSmall transport; identity-edge epimorphism argument written by J1
